annotations.text:
ONE DOOR — what consolidates

One tile. On a phone the body opens the camera and the small Gallery pill opens the photo library; on a desktop the body picks files and takes a drop. Two tiles become one.

One card. A typed product is the same card without a photo, on this page. The separate nine-field form goes; product type, SEO and files stay on the edit page, where they already live.

More, inside the card: category chips and a description, opening in place. Two things, not nine. A filled category shows on the closed row.

Fill it in: the AI snap page becomes a pill on the photo, shown only when AI is on. It writes the name, category and description, and the amber line says so.

Upload a spreadsheet opens the existing CSV sheet on this page, not on Products.

Products page: one button, Add products.

TODAY

Two buttons on the Products page, four on this one. Three of the six lead to pages in the old style: the nine-field form, the AI snap page, the CSV sheet on the Products list. A merchant meets three different pages for one job, and the desktop page is two tiles and empty space.

ALTERNATE — grow the shelf (low-fi)

No add page at all. The camera tile is the first tile on the Products page; new photos land as amber draft tiles at the top, get a name and a price where they stand, and turn into products in place.

For: the merchant never leaves the list, and the shop grows in front of them.

Against: thirty photos flood the list, and the list page has to carry uploads, card states and a publish bar. Typed products and spreadsheets still need a home.
